q: Is the 20-minute-gap Table-S1 row (A=100.9, B=0.69) a genuine biological outlier, a unit/typo error, or evidence that the two-exposure offset-sum model (Eq. 4) breaks down at very short inter-exposure intervals?
basis: Two independent pass-2 tests (T-6 height 62.97 vs paper ~30 foci/cell; T-8 net-foci 24.5 > single-acute 21.8, which is mechanistically impossible for refractory cells) both fail on exactly this row. It is the single unresolved anomaly gating the verdict from EXCEEDED to REPLICATED.
next_steps: Refit the 20-min condition directly from the digitized Fig-5A points (independent of Table S1) and compare the refit A/B to the published row; if the refit lands near ~30 foci, the Table-S1 row is a typo. If not, test whether a saturating (rather than additive) second-exposure induction term is required at gaps below the ~0.5 h foci-formation timescale.

q: Does the offset-sum superposition assumption (Eq. 4: second exposure adds an independent, time-shifted copy of the induction/decay kernel) hold mechanistically, or is there genuine kinetic coupling (repair-protein depletion, chromatin remodeling) between the two DSB populations?
basis: The model reproduces 4/5 split-dose conditions by assuming the second exposure's foci evolve independently of residual first-exposure foci. The paper's own narrative ('repair significantly slower if 2nd occurs within 5 h', confirmed as T-5) implies coupling the additive model does not encode.
next_steps: Build a coupled two-compartment repair model where the second exposure's decay rate is a function of residual first-exposure foci load, refit all 5 split-dose curves, and use AIC/BIC to test whether the coupled model is statistically justified over the additive one given the data resolution.

q: How identifiable are the 5 fit parameters (A,B,C,D,E) of Eqs. (3)-(4) from the available foci-time data, and are the published Table-S1 values a unique minimum or one of many near-equivalent fits?
basis: Pass-1 already flagged identifiability weakness (equivalent-RMSE refits exist), and T-5's anomalous 5-h-gap decay rate (0.386, faster not slower) is consistent with a flat/degenerate objective landscape rather than a real kinetic effect.
next_steps: Run a profile-likelihood / MCMC parameter-uncertainty analysis on each of the 7 fits, report confidence intervals and parameter correlations, and quantify how many time points (and at what times) would be needed to make B and E individually identifiable.

q: Does the ~25 foci/cell/Gy induction yield (T-1, reproduced at 20.1) generalize across radiation qualities (30 kVp, MeV photons, ions), or is it specific to 225 kVp X-rays, and what is the LET dependence of the split-dose recovery kinetics?
basis: T-1 was reproduced within 20% but only for 225 kVp. The paper reports 30 kVp and clonogenic data but Table S1 gives no 30-kVp fit parameters, so no cross-quality test was possible in this replication (§6).
next_steps: Digitize the Fig-2 30-kVp foci curves, fit Eq. (3), and compare induction yield and decay half-lives to the 225-kVp values; then test whether split-dose recovery times scale with initial DSB complexity (LET) by extending to the sibling ion-beam LUCID datasets.

q: Can the split-dose gamma-H2AX recovery timescale (~1 h needed for two resolved peaks; recovery to baseline by 12 h) be mapped onto clinical fractionation intervals to predict a foci-based optimal inter-fraction time, and does it agree with LQ-derived repair half-times?
basis: T-2/T-7/T-8 established that 12-h gaps recover to fresh-single-acute behaviour and >=1-h gaps yield two peaks. This is a directly actionable foci-kinetics result but the paper stops at the assay level without translating to fractionation guidance.
next_steps: Convert the fitted foci decay half-times to an equivalent LQ Lea-Catcheside repair half-time, compare against clinical tissue-specific values (e.g. ~1.5 h for late-responding tissue), and test whether foci-kinetics predict the same inter-fraction interval as survival-based models on a shared cell line.
